contradictions.fact: Descent time from summit to trailhead

claims.says: Descent time is roughly 5 hours (about 1.5 hours from summit to Rainy Lake, 2+ hours from the lake back to the car)
Summit break ends ~11:00-11:30 AM; Back at Rainy Lake ~1:00 PM; Back at trailhead ~3:00 PM

contradictions.why: descent_text's own two sub-splits (1.5 hr + 2 hr = 3.5 hr) don't add up to its stated headline 'roughly 5 hours', and the itinerary schedule (summit break end ~11:15 AM to trailhead 3:00 PM) independently shows only ~3.5-4 hours of descent, not 5.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The itinerary schedule and descent_text's own sub-times agree with each other at ~3.5-4 hrs; the headline 'roughly 5 hours' in descent_text is the outlier.

distMi: 4.3

claims.says: Late July through September-July-October season

contradictions.why: The optimal-window sentence appears to merge two different season strings into one garbled, internally contradictory phrase (reads as spanning both 'late July-September' and 'July-October' at once, out of order).

contradictions.fact: Approach trailhead/route named in partner_requirements (Taylor River vs Green Ridge)

claims.says: hike in via the Taylor River / Snoqualmie Lake trail system, then leave the trail for an unmarked, brushy scramble route to the summit
roughly 10+ miles round trip with several thousand feet of gain
Unsigned climbers' path off FS Road 56 ... about 1.1 miles before the Dingford Creek Trailhead (Green Ridge line)
Don't mistake the old Taylor River approach (via the washed-out bridge area) for the current standard route — it adds many extra miles

contradictions.why: partner_requirements describes the OLD Taylor River/Snoqualmie Lake approach and a 10+ mile round trip, which the route's own watch_out field explicitly warns is NOT the current standard route (the ~7 mi Green Ridge/FS 56 line documented in approach, road, waypoints, and approach_variants).
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, approach_logistics, road, waypoints, approach_variants, and watch_out all independently agree on the Green Ridge/FS 56 climbers' path (~7 mi RT); partner_requirements is the sole outlier and appears to carry over stale Taylor River approach text.

contradictions.fact: Season window vs seasonal_guidance's 'optimal' window

claims.says: Jun-Sep (climbable as a snow/scramble route in winter/spring with traction gear and added avalanche/cornice hazard)
Mid-July through September is the reliable weather and snow-free window
Mid-July through October, with the core dry-and-stable window in August-September
good
Late July to September

contradictions.why: season and best_season both cap the reliable window at September, but seasonal_guidance calls October part of the 'optimal' window and rates it 'good' — a month outside the stated season, not merely a narrower best-window inside a wider one.

contradictions.fact: Total elevation gain (gain_ft vs itinerary's net gain vs prose)

claims.says: about 4,400 ft net gain, though real trip reports log 5,500-6,100+ ft of total up-and-down
total climbing (not just net gain) is closer to 6,000 ft round trip

contradictions.why: The header/Overview TECHNICAL STATS will show gain_ft=6500 while the Plan tab's itinerary TOTAL row shows only 4400 (net gain) for the same climb, and the route's own prose gives yet other totals (5,500-6,100+ and 'closer to 6,000') - none matching 6500 - so a climber sees several different total-gain numbers.
contradictions.internal_resolution: 4400 is explainable as the net trailhead-to-summit elevation change (1,350 to 5,765 ft, confirmed by waypoints); the true cumulative gain including the ~800 ft mid-route drop-and-regain is closer to the 5,500-6,100 ft the prose describes, making the header's 6,500 the likely outlier.

contradictions.fact: Round-trip distance (dist_km vs itinerary miles)

claims.says: distMi 3.8 (one-way, implying ~7.6 mi round trip)

contradictions.why: dist_km converts to about 4.5 mi, well under the ~7-7.6 mi round trip implied by the itinerary and the doubled one-way waypoint mileage; flagged low priority per the dist_km one-way/round-trip convention note.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary miles (7) and doubled waypoint one-way distance (~7.6) agree with each other; dist_km (4.5 mi) is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Whether a self-issue permit is required/exists on this DNR land

claims.says: None required — free self-issue day-use permit at the trailhead (no quota for day use).
This peak is not inside the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, so the USFS wilderness group-size limit and self-issue wilderness permit do not apply here; a Discover Pass is required to park at the trailhead.
No climbing permit; a Discover Pass is required to park on Washington State lands.

contradictions.why: access.permit both says a permit is 'None required' and then describes a free self-issue day-use permit as if it exists, and that description directly contradicts access.rules' explicit statement that self-issue permits 'do not apply here' on this DNR (non-Wilderness) land.
contradictions.internal_resolution: access.rules and the top-level permit field agree no self-issue permit exists on this DNR land (only a Discover Pass to park); access.permit's mention of a self-issue day-use permit is the outlier and matches the sibling Standard Route's access.permit, which correctly states no self-issue permit box exists.

contradictions.fact: Hardest pitch grade / crux grade disagreement

claims.says: 5.2 (5.5 at the overhanging band)
grade 5.1-5.6
about 400 ft of the route's pleasant climbing is 4th to easy 5th class, with the notable overhanging band rated 5.5

contradictions.why: The route's headline grade is 5.2, rock_grade calls the crux '5.5', but pitch_detail's P1 grade range tops out at 5.6 — three different numbers for the route's hardest move, and no pitch in pitch_detail is actually labeled 5.5.

contradictions.fact: Total elevation loss (loss_ft vs itinerary day's lossFt)
contradictions.why: This is a single-day out-and-back from the same trailhead, so the day's loss should equal the route's total loss_ft (which equals gain_ft, 3138); the itinerary's 2600 is about 17% short of that.

contradictions.fact: Ice grade (route-level ice_grade vs crux pitch grades)

claims.says: AI2
grade AI3
grade AI3

contradictions.why: The header/Overview grade chip shows ice_grade 'AI2', but the route's own crux pitches (P1, marked crux:true, and P4) are graded AI3 in pitch_detail — a full grade harder than the headline.
contradictions.internal_resolution: pitch_detail's own P1/P4 entries (both AI3) show the technical difficulty is AI3, not AI2; the top-level ice_grade appears to understate it.

contradictions.fact: Crux step angle (max_angle/pitch_detail vs beta/pro_tips/waypoint)

claims.says: Steepens again to 50-70° snow and ice on the final headwall
one short crux step that can approach 80° (sometimes rock, 5.4-5.6, if thin on ice)
The crux is a short (~10 ft) step below the summit block that can hit ~80°
a crux step up to roughly 80 degrees (occasionally bare 5.6 rock) leads to the summit from here

contradictions.why: max_angle and pitch_detail cap the steepest ice/snow at 70°, but beta, pro_tips, and the col waypoint all independently describe a short crux step reaching about 80° — a notably steeper, more serious move than max_angle states.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Three independent prose fields (beta, pro_tips, waypoint note) agree on ~80°; max_angle and pitch_detail's P4 range are the outliers.

contradictions.fact: Total approach gain to the base of the North Face

claims.says: Total approach gain to the base is roughly 1,300-1,500 ft over about 2.5-3 miles one-way

claims.field: waypoints (Alpental TH elev 3100 -> North Face open-book base elev 5506)
claims.says: implies ~2,406 ft of gain over that same one-way stretch

contradictions.why: The approach prose's stated total gain to the base (1,300-1,500 ft) is roughly 900-1,100 ft less than the elevation difference between the route's own trailhead (3,100 ft) and base (5,506 ft) waypoints - a gap large enough to materially misstate the approach's effort/time.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoints (with explicit elev/elevFt values matching the route's other gain figures) are self-consistent; the approach text's 1,300-1,500 ft figure is the likely outlier, possibly measuring only the final leg from the ~4,200 ft basin rather than the true trailhead-to-base total.

contradictions.fact: Hardest rock grade (route grade vs rock_grade vs pitch_detail)

claims.says: Class 5.6
grade AI2-3 (winter) / 5.4-5.6 (dry)
about 400 ft of mostly Class 3-4 with one short 5.6 step

contradictions.why: The header grade pill (rock_grade takes priority) would show '5.4,' a full grade below the route's own stated crux difficulty of 5.6 (used in the grade field, P3's dry range, and pro_tips).
contradictions.internal_resolution: grade, P3's dry range, and pro_tips all agree the crux is 5.6; rock_grade (5.4) understates it and is the likely outlier.

claims.says: totaling a 5-8 hour car-to-car day
About 2 hours from the Alpental/Snow Lake trailhead to the base of the buttress
+3.5 hr Reach base of the Northeast Buttress ... One detailed trip report logged 3 hr 24 min car-to-base
about 10-12 hours; one well-documented trip logged 11 hr 22 min total

contradictions.why: partner_requirements gives a much shorter car-to-car time (5-8 hrs) and approach time (~2 hrs) than every other time field on the route (totalHrs 11.5, the schedule, and totalNote's logged 11h22m trip / 3h24m approach) - a climber using the Partners tab to gauge commitment would badly underestimate the day.
contradictions.internal_resolution: timing, the itinerary schedule, and totalNote all agree closely (~10-12 hrs total, ~3.5 hr approach) citing a real logged trip report; partner_requirements is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Getting-there road/access describe a different, unrelated area

claims.says: Alpental Road, Snoqualmie Pass (I-90 Exit 52), for The Citadel
Roughly 45 min-1 hour from Seattle via I-90 to Exit 52.
Reiter Foothills / Gold Bar bouldering area
Washington Department of Natural Resources (DNR managed land near Gold Bar)
From I-90 Exit 54 (Hyak), follow Hyak Drive onto Forest Service Road NF-9070 ... (Silver Basin, National Forest)

contradictions.why: The GETTING THERE (road) and ACCESS fields describe two entirely different, unrelated climbing areas - Alpental/The Citadel off I-90 Exit 52, and the DNR Reiter Foothills bouldering area near Gold Bar - neither of which is Silver Basin/The Obelisk, which the route's own approach, waypoints, and overview place off I-90 Exit 54 via Hyak Drive/FR-9070 on National Forest land. A climber following road/access as written would drive to the wrong trailhead and expect the wrong pass/permit.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, waypoints, and overview all independently agree on Hyak/FR-9070/Silver Basin; road and access appear contaminated with unrelated areas' data.

contradictions.fact: Protection style: bolted sport route vs trad rack/rope_note

claims.says: Fully bolted sport protection throughout; no gear placements required.
a 2-pitch bolted sport line ... follows the obvious, continuous bolt line
cams: standard Index trad rack up to #4 (Camalot-equivalent); nuts: standard nut set; runners: 4-6 slings
Presumed short trad route on Index Town Wall granite (Obelisk/Madsen's Ledge area); standard 60m rope to lower/rappel.

contradictions.why: The route is described everywhere else (overview, beta, pitch_detail, pro_needs, detailed_rack) as a fully bolted 2-pitch sport route needing no gear, but sling_rack lists a full trad rack and rope_note calls it a 'trad route' at Index Town Wall - a different crag entirely, unrelated to Silver Basin.
contradictions.internal_resolution: overview, beta, pitch_detail, pro_needs, and detailed_rack all agree this is bolted sport climbing; sling_rack and rope_note appear copied from an unrelated Index Town Wall trad route.

contradictions.fact: The Obelisk's own elevation disagreement across waypoints

claims.says: elev 4494
elev 4494
elev 4900, note: 'Elevation is an estimate from the surrounding terrain ... no separate elevation figure is published for this formation.'

contradictions.why: Three waypoints for the same named formation ('The Obelisk') give two different elevations (4494 ft twice, 4900 ft once) - a ~400 ft (9%) disagreement about the crag's own height.
